chunks: Abu al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Jayd al-Qummi informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim al-Khazzaz, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Awwad, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
If you are leading a people, one taslim to your right suffices for you. If you are with an Imam, then two taslims. And if you are alone, then one, while facing the qiblah.

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader being followed in congregational salat
key_terms.تَؤُمُّ: you lead the people in prayer
key_terms.تَسْلِيمَةٌ: a single utterance of taslim concluding the prayer

ai.seo_question: How should taslim be performed in salat when leading, following an Imam, or praying alone?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of taslim in salat according to one's role in the prayer. It distinguishes between the one leading the congregation, the one praying behind an Imam, and the one praying alone, indicating how many taslims are sufficient in each case.
